title: An agent has a 200k token context budget per session, $0.50 per session cost cap, and must reason over a 1M-token codebase. Pick one retrieval architecture and defend the cost/recall trade-off.
description:
Concrete situation: building a code-review agent. Per-session budget is 200k tokens (input + output) and $0.50. Target codebase is ~1M tokens. The agent must answer a single review question per session referencing arbitrary code anywhere in the repo. Recall threshold (must find the relevant file) is the hard requirement; precision (only retrieving relevant chunks) is soft.

Name ONE retrieval architecture and defend it on three axes:

1. **Architecture** — be specific: chunk size, embedding model, top-K, reranker yes/no, full-file vs snippet, any hierarchy. Acceptable: "512-token AST-aware chunks, BGE-large embeddings, top-50 vector → BM25 rerank top-10 → return surrounding 3 chunks". Unacceptable: "RAG with embeddings".

2. **Token + dollar math** — fit a single session under both 200k tokens and $0.50. Show: chunks retrieved × tokens per chunk + reasoning tokens + output tokens; embedding API cost or self-host cost amortized. Round, but justify orders of magnitude.

3. **Recall failure case** — name ONE class of question your architecture WILL miss, and the cost to close that gap. Examples: a question that depends on a comment that survives chunking but not embedding semantics; a question requiring three-hop reference resolution.

Common bait answers:
- "Just stuff the whole codebase." 1M > 200k. Don't.
- "Use the longest-context model and skip retrieval." Above the dollar cap. Show the math if you propose this.
- "Use multiple agents." Out of scope — one session, one architecture.

Voters: judge on (a) architecture specificity (exact mechanism, not 'embeddings + LLM'), (b) the math actually fits both caps, (c) the named failure mode is real and the gap-closing cost is sensible.

success_criteria.name: specific_architecture
success_criteria.description: Names chunk size + embedding choice + top-K + rerank/no + retrieval shape. Generic 'RAG' fails.

success_criteria.name: fits_both_caps
success_criteria.description: Math demonstrates the architecture fits BOTH 200k token + $0.50 caps. Order-of-magnitude OK with numbers; 'should fit' fails.

success_criteria.name: named_failure_class
success_criteria.description: Names ONE concrete class of question the architecture misses, plus cost-to-close estimate. 'Some edge cases' fails.
